title: Producing an export bundle and restoring from one
summary: A streamed ZIP of every durable collection with per-file checksums, and the privileged restore that verifies all of them before it writes a single row.
note: The two halves have different front doors and that asymmetry is real, not a drawing simplification. Export is an authenticated HTTP route the browser calls. Restore has NO route: restoreBundle is reached only from the CLI script apps/api/src/scripts/restore.ts, run by an operator against an extracted directory with the API env pointed at the target database. The share-safe export (includeSensitive false) is deliberately not restorable: restore.ts:61 refuses it outright, because entire collections come back as empty files.

actors.label: Browser (Export page)
actors.note: Uses api.download, which carries the bearer token, the session cookie and the data-space header, with a ten-minute timeout because the stream is legitimately slow.

actors.label: export router
actors.note: Streams the ZIP entry by entry. A per-workspace in-process lock refuses a concurrent export.

actors.label: export service
actors.note: An async generator: one collection or vault note at a time, paged from Postgres, hashed incrementally. The full database is never in memory at once.

actors.label: Postgres
actors.note: Walked id-ordered with keyset paging (id > last), 500 rows at a time. Not OFFSET, which would re-scan the prefix on every page.

actors.label: Object storage
actors.note: Attachment bytes. Streamed into the bundle one object at a time and re-hashed on the way through.

actors.label: Operator (CLI)
actors.note: Runs `pnpm --filter @vitae/api restore <dir> [--force]` against an extracted bundle. There is no HTTP restore.

actors.label: restore service
actors.note: Verifies manifest, checksums, counts, referential integrity and blob hashes before the first write.

steps.label: POST /api/v1/export { includeSensitive }
steps.note: Passing the flow's own gate first: this is one of the routes the entitlement gate still allows while a workspace is read-only, so a lapsed account can always get its data out.

steps.label: 409 EXPORT_IN_PROGRESS
steps.note: A per-workspace Set held in process memory (FR-105). It does not serialize across instances; cross-instance exclusion would need a shared lease.

steps.label: open the ZIP stream, then pull entries from the generator
steps.note: The archive is piped to the response immediately; an aborted request aborts the archive rather than leaving it writing into a dead socket.

steps.label: page each collection, drop sensitive records transitively
steps.note: Exclusion follows references: an edge touching a sensitive node, an atom owned by one, its variants and skills, its revisions, reminders, taggings and merges all go with it. Policy checks re-read the referenced record instead of holding collection-sized maps.

steps.label: hash every JSONL file incrementally as it is produced
steps.note: Each line is `{_doc_id, ...data}` so a restore can put every document back under its original id. Secrets are scrubbed regardless of source: the GitHub PAT is stripped from the meta row.

steps.label: stream attachment bytes into blobs/<sha> (complete backups only)
steps.note: Re-hashed while streaming; a checksum or byte-count mismatch throws mid-export rather than producing a bundle that only looks complete. Without includeSensitive, blobs is 0 and targets/resumes/letters/imports/meta are empty files.

steps.label: manifest.json last: schema_version, counts, checksums, blobs
steps.note: The manifest is both the final entry and the generator's return value, so the route can record last_export_at and the counts without re-reading the archive.

steps.label: application/zip stream, then persist the export status doc
restore <extracted-bundle-dir> [--force]
steps.note: Files are read off disk by the script; blobs/* stay Buffers and everything else becomes UTF-8 text.

steps.label: RestoreError: unsupported schema_version, or a share-safe bundle
steps.note: Only 3.x is understood; older bundles do not guarantee complete subcollection and blob recovery. A bundle without includes_sensitive is refused because it is intentionally incomplete.

steps.label: verify: every required file present, SHA-256 matches the manifest, counts match
steps.note: This is the integrity boundary. All of it runs before the first write, so a corrupt bundle cannot half-land. Optional collections (letters, dedup_aliases) may be absent but are still parsed when present.

steps.label: RestoreError: checksum mismatch, count mismatch, or a dangling reference
steps.note: Counts are checked at restore.ts:82 and in-bundle referential integrity from restore.ts:109: an edge whose src or dst is not among the bundle's nodes, a variant without its atom, an import row without its import.

steps.label: count every collection; refuse a non-empty database unless --force
verify every blob's size and SHA-256, then upload them all
steps.note: Verification of the whole blob set completes before any upload, and the new storage keys are remapped onto the attachment rows as they are written.

steps.label: bulk upsert every document under its original id, then prune stale rows if --force
steps.note: --force is a non-destructive upsert-then-prune, never a truncate: a failed restore can be rerun safely and never begins by emptying the only copy. A collection the bundle does not carry is skipped rather than pruned to empty.

steps.label: { collections, total } after publishing a search invalidation
